goal: Compare the methods reported in the three uploaded papers with experiment.xlsx results. Find the best configuration under 3M parameters, generate a chart, and assess whether our results support the reported design advantages. Use only uploaded data and documents; these are synthetic fixtures.
answer:
## Comparison of reported methods and `experiment.xlsx`

| Model | Reported method | Params (M) | Reported mIoU | Under `<3M`? |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| A | Convolutional segmentation | 2.5 | 73.27 | Yes — best eligible [Analysis dc98b54c-961a-43d6-b64a-3dd252e192e4] |
| B | Attention segmentation | 3.2 | 76.0 | No — exceeds budget [Analysis dc98b54c-961a-43d6-b64a-3dd252e192e4] |
| C | Compact convolution baseline | 2.0 | 70.0 | Yes [Analysis dc98b54c-961a-43d6-b64a-3dd252e192e4] |

Reported method labels: A [paper_1.pdf, p.1], B [paper_2.pdf, p.1], C [paper_3.pdf, p.1]. `experiment.xlsx` has three rows with columns `model`, `params_m`, `miou`; its sampled values match A/B/C exactly [Analysis f72fbc74-84e6-4e0b-9f2d-54728facce1a].

## Best configuration under 3M parameters

Using the computed `rank_under_budget` operation with strict constraint `< 3.0M`, the best eligible configuration is **Method A: 2.5M parameters, mIoU 73.27** [Analysis dc98b54c-961a-43d6-b64a-3dd252e192e4]. Eligible: A and C; B is excluded at 3.2M [Analysis dc98b54c-961a-43d6-b64a-3dd252e192e4]. Ranking by mIoU: B (76.0), A (73.27), C (70.0); B is not eligible under the stated budget [Analysis dc98b54c-961a-43d6-b64a-3dd252e192e4].

## Chart

The analysis output records chart `comparison.png` [Analysis dc98b54c-961a-43d6-b64a-3dd252e192e4]. The evidence shown does not include a visual inspection of that chart.

## Do our results support the reported design advantages?

The `experiment.xlsx` values mirror the paper-reported fixture values: A 2.5M / 73.27, B 3.2M / 76.0, C 2.0M / 70.0 [Analysis f72fbc74-84e6-4e0b-9f2d-54728facce1a][paper_1.pdf, p.1][paper_2.pdf, p.1][paper_3.pdf, p.1]. They are consistent with the reported **descriptive quality/cost tradeoff**: A improves over C by 3.27 mIoU at +0.5M parameters, and B improves over A by 2.73 mIoU at +0.7M parameters [paper_1.pdf, p.1][paper_2.pdf, p.1][paper_3.pdf, p.1].

They do **not** independently validate architectural design advantage. The cited sources explicitly describe only descriptive quality/cost tradeoffs with no causal or ablation claim, no uncertainty estimates, and no additional configurations [paper_3.pdf, p.1]. Under the 3M constraint, Method B’s higher mIoU is inaccessible; the supported constrained choice remains Method A [Analysis dc98b54c-961a-43d6-b64a-3dd252e192e4].

## Limits and gaps

The cited evidence does not include architecture/training details, dataset-level metrics beyond these descriptive statistics/ranking, uncertainty, ablations, or additional configurations [Analysis f72fbc74-84e6-4e0b-9f2d-54728facce1a][paper_3.pdf, p.1]. The values are synthetic fixtures, not published research claims [paper_1.pdf, p.1][paper_2.pdf, p.1][paper_3.pdf, p.1].
